tasks.description: gap G-STAGE-01: reconcile the three coexisting job-stage vocabularies (main.ts STAGES, jobState.ts JobStage, stage.ts's own STAGES) against lib/workflow/state.ts's unadopted unification
tasks.assignedWorker: claude — audit first (is state.ts a strict superset?), then migrate only if genuinely safe
tasks.outputs: RESOLVED 2026-08-25: documented decision to KEEP the three vocabularies as-is, not migrate yet, after performing the exact audit docs/MASTER_CAPABILITY_TOOL_REGISTRY.json's G-STAGE-01 asked for ('audit whether state.ts's vocabulary is a strict superset of the three live ones before any adoption'). Finding: it is NOT a superset -- lib/workflow/state.ts's 12 states use deliberately abstract names (verify/judge/decide) that state.ts's own docstring already explains are meant to CONTAIN jobState.ts's 17 concrete stages as sub-steps (e.g. 'browser' + 'visual-critic' + 'distinctness-gate' would fold into 'verify'/'judge'/'decide'), not rename them 1:1. Only 3 of jobState.ts's 17 names (created/evidence/diverge) and 1 of stage.ts's 23 names (diverge) match state.ts's vocabulary by exact string -- confirming this is a real semantic remapping design task, not a mechanical find-replace, and confirming the registry's caution was correct. The three vocabularies also serve three genuinely different, currently load-bearing purposes verified by reading each: main.ts's 9 STAGES are the deterministic CLI pipeline's step names; jobState.ts's 17 JobStage values are the persisted production job.json contract that WQ-016's control surface (STAGE_LABELS/STAGE_ORDER in controlSurfacePage.ts) and the n8n GET /job HTTP contract (test/qa/p7-endpoints.test.ts) both already depend on; scripts/n8n/stage.ts's 23 STAGES are the legacy per-stage HTTP dispatch keys (GET/POST /stage/:name) used by the CLI and Factory V1. A real migration would need to simultaneously: (1) design the concrete-to-abstract state mapping, (2) write a back-compat reader for every existing on-disk job.json (old stage names), (3) update the control surface and n8n workflow generator in lockstep so neither silently breaks. That is a genuine, carefully-planned multi-file migration, not something to fold into this checkpoint -- follow-up WQ-019 queued with these exact prerequisites as its scope. lib/workflow/state.ts is kept as-is (not deprecated): it is the correct target semantic model, just not yet an adoptable one.

tasks.assignedWorker: claude to investigate; this is a product/architecture DECISION the mandate authorizes me to make, not one requiring human sign-off, but it is high-blast-radius (changes what a run actually produces) so it gets its own careful pass rather than a rushed tail-end change
tasks.outputs: DECISION (2026-08-25): Design Battle stays deliberately opt-in scaffolding, not the production default, for three concrete reasons found by reading both code paths side by side (lib/forge/orchestrator.ts's runExperienceForge vs lib/forge/battle.ts's runExperienceBattle), not a generic caution: (1) runExperienceForge has a real autonomous repair loop (repairCode, up to maxIterations) after the first critique; runExperienceBattle builds each candidate in exactly one pass with no repair step at all -- wiring it in today would mean every battle-selected site skips repair entirely, a quality regression dressed as a feature, not an improvement. (2) Cost multiplies by candidateCount (default 2) with zero integration into lib/capability/budget.ts's resolveBudgetTier -- the existing per-job budget ceiling (job.budgetCents) would not see or bound battle spend. (3) JobState's designDirections/distinctnessScore fields are already the classic lib/design/diverge.ts battle's fields (see lib/workflow/summary.ts's summarizeBattle, wired in WQ-016) -- reusing them for Forge's separate battle.ts would conflate two different mechanisms in the one-read-model control surface this session just built, corrupting it rather than extending it. None of these are reasons to deprecate battle.ts (the structural-convergence reuse is sound and the module is well-tested) -- they are concrete missing prerequisites. Follow-up WQ-018 queued with those exact prerequisites as its scope, so the eventual wiring is a real quality upgrade, not a cost/quality regression shipped under a feature name.

Researched current browser support first (caniuse.com, webkit.org -- OBSERVED 2026-08-25: animation-timeline: scroll()/view() at 85.43% global support, Chrome 115+/Firefox 157+/Safari 26.0+ -- no longer experimental). tasks.outputs: Implemented: menu-overlay's open/close (lib/runtime/forgePrimitives.ts MENU_OVERLAY_SOURCE) is wrapped in document.startViewTransition() when supported (`if (document.startViewTransition)`) and prefers-reduced-motion is not set (`matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`, computed once up front). The pre-existing attribute-flip logic (applyOpen) is unconditional in both branches -- unsupported browsers and reduced-motion visitors get byte-for-byte the same behaviour as before. CSS (MENU_OVERLAY_RULES) tags only the overlay element (`view-transition-name: forge-menu-overlay`, scoped inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`) to avoid the implicit full-viewport root snapshot crossfade a bare startViewTransition() call would otherwise trigger on every toggle. `::view-transition-group(forge-menu-overlay)` duration/easing (360ms ease) match the existing CSS transition on the same element. Deliberately did not attempt custom ::view-transition-old/new keyframes to replicate the translateY slide -- the default opacity crossfade already reproduces the existing fade correctly in both directions (the closed state is opacity:0/visibility:hidden, so it always renders blank on its side of the crossfade) and getting open-vs-close direction right for a custom keyframe pair without a real cross-browser visual test carried real regression risk for already-shipped code. 9 new tests (4 integration in test/render/runtimePrimitives.integration.test.ts, 5 registry in test/design/experienceRegistry.test.ts) prove: feature-detection + reduced-motion gating ordering, the fallback path is unconditional/unchanged, view-transition-name is correctly scoped, inertness without the base runtime, registry entry validity, and that deriveRuntimePrimitives still never auto-selects menu-overlay. Full suite: 1490 tests, 1486 passing, 4 known Playwright-dependent sandbox-only failures (unrelated pre-existing baseline). docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GAP.md P2-2 and docs/MASTER_CAPABILITY_TOOL_REGISTRY.json's runtime.menu-overlay entry updated to document the enhancement; P2-2 is now fully RESOLVED (both WQ-021 and WQ-022 halves complete).
